construction: For a selected cell use R=OwnedCell intersect ClosedOrderRegion(rho), preserving its Ico ownership and both weak ordering walls.
Use a common prime cube [h/2,rho+1). R lies in this cube because z>=lo2>=h and x>=y>=z, while all actual dyadic upper endpoints are <=rho.

Apply tendsto_actualPrimeBoxTestSum_cube_affineSandwich directly, rather than pretending the shifted common cube has the same dyadic grid. The eight nonzero forms are the six actual coordinate lower/upper rows plus y-x and z-y. The strict region is contained in R; R satisfies the eight weak rows pointwise. This retains arithmetic atoms on weak walls.

The prime test measure has density product_i 1/t_i. Use profile 4*(oldLowerFactor-newLowerFactor)/z, with z continuously clamped below by h/2 outside the cube. On R, multiplication by the three reciprocal coordinate densities gives exactly the existing CapKernel with denominator x*y*z^2.

The physical cell level is constant in N and the canonical clamped lower factor is continuous. The positive common lower bound pays all denominators. A finite sum then gives the corresponding fixed compact harmonic correction limit.
The compact functional theorem chooses h,e,m before N. It permits positive e; uniformity at e=0 is not an arithmetic license to use zero buffer.
